verdicts.reason: Both lose the can's fill. It is a faint orange outline on orange, and the cream circle that framed it is stranded at the bottom-left, half off the canvas. A keeps a clear two-column split, but its NEW pill sits alone in the top-right corner and Try It is not aligned to the headline's left edge. B's NEW pill floats between the subhead and the CTA on its own axis, and the CTA doesn't line up with the copy either, so its right column is more scattered.

A has the shared flaws: the can is reduced to an invisible outline, the cream circle is orphaned at the bottom-left, and the NEW badge is isolated in the corner. B is worse. The can is shrunk to a tiny scrap, the Try It CTA is shrunk until its label can't be read and pushed off to the right, NEW floats at the bottom centre, and the headline, subhead and CTA all sit on different edges.

A flips the layout to text-left. Its NEW pill shrinks to an unreadable chip floating in the gutter, and Try It sits right on top of the orphaned cream circle in a near-collision. The can outline is still barely visible. B keeps an orderly two-column layout, though the can is still a faint outline, the cream circle is detached and the CTA is misaligned with the copy.

A is the same two-column layout as before, with the same flaws: a faint can outline, a stranded cream circle, a corner NEW pill and a misaligned CTA. B is unusable. The product is shrunk to a speck, the CTA and NEW are shrunk until their labels can't be read and huddle at the bottom, and the headline and subhead float with huge dead space around them, so the hierarchy is gone.
